reasons: Lake identity gives case_name "Cardwell v. Lewis", court "U.S. Supreme Court", date_decided "1974-06-17", and year 1974.
Lake citations list official "417 U.S. 583", parallels "94 S. Ct. 2464", "41 L. Ed. 2d 325", "69 Ohio Op. 2d 69", and vendor cite "1974 U.S. LEXIS 75".
The opinion expressly frames the case as involving "a warrantless seizure of an automobile and the examination of its exterior".
The opinion discusses the Carroll-Chambers automobile line and says less stringent warrant requirements have generally applied to vehicles.
residual_risks: The search-and-seizure rationale is plurality-only, so any stronger use than a related home role should be caveated.

reasons: The opinion grounds the analysis in Fourth Amendment privacy, stating that "the primary object of the Fourth Amendment was determined to be the protection of privacy".
It states that one has a lesser expectation of privacy in a motor vehicle and asks what expectation of privacy was infringed by the exterior examination.
residual_risks: The reasonable-expectation rationale is from the plurality opinion.

defect.evidence_quote: MR. JUSTICE BLACKMUN announced the judgment of the Court and an opinion in which the CHIEF JUSTICE, MR. JUSTICE WHITE, and MR. JUSTICE REHNQUIST join.
defect.problem: The substantive rule is supported by the plurality text, but the assertion is framed as the case holding without stating that only four Justices joined the Fourth Amendment rationale and Powell concurred only in the result.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the holding field to say the plurality reasoned that, where probable cause exists, warrantless examination of a car's exterior, after seizure from a public lot and later impoundment, was not unreasonable because the privacy invasion was minimal/the vehicle exterior carried a reduced expectation of privacy.

reasons: The opinion supports the exterior-examination proposition: "where probable cause exists, a warrantless examination of the exterior of a car is not unreasonable under the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments."
The opinion also supports reduced vehicle privacy: "One has a lesser expectation of privacy in a motor vehicle".
But disclosed text and lake scope note show this was a plurality opinion, with Powell concurring in the result on a different ground.
residual_risks: The proposition should not be used as an uncaveated majority holding from Cardwell itself.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use "plurality" or "plurality rationale" in the holding/rule text, not just in treatment metadata.

residual_risks: The case-level binding label does not by itself make the plurality rationale a majority holding.
